sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:143282
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 27017 of 2023

Applicant :- Tinku
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Jai Karan Nath
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Jai Karan Nath, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Manav Chaurasiya, learned
Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
84 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 IPC & 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Saifani, District Rampur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased about four years before and after marriage, applicant and his family members tortured the deceased for want of jewellery and a car and on 14.7.2022, informant received an information that applicant and his family members committed the murder of her daughter i.e deceased.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that when informant arrived at the village of applicant then she received information that after committing murder of her daughter, she was cremated.

Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62626274/
1 4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry, he has been made accused in the present matter and actually, deceased died due to corona and this fact was immediately informed by applicant to the informant and other family members of the deceased and after their permission, he started cremation but in the meantime, informant arrived at the time of her cremation and started making demand of Rs. Seven lacs and when applicant failed to fulfil their demand then on the basis offalse allegation, FIR of the present case was lodged.
5.

He further submitted that although on the complaint made by the informant, half burnt dead body of the deceased was recovered and thereafter post mortem of the dead body of the of the deceased was conducted and according to the post mortem report cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera was preserved.
6. He further submitted that although he could not annex the viscera report alongwith the instant bail application but no poison was found in the viscera report.
He further submitted that as no poison was found, therefore, it is not a case of abnormal death and defence taken by the applicant that deceased died due to corona appears to be quite probable.
7. He next submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 17.7.2022 i.e. for last one year, therefore, he may be released on bail.

8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that according to the viscera report, no poison was found.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Although, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home and there was allegation of demand of dowry and also allegation against the applicant is that he without informing the informant tried to dispose of the death body of the deceased but from the record, it reflects that at the time of cremation, informant arrived at spot and on his compliant half burnt dead body of the deceased was recovered and thereafter post mortem of the dead body was conducted and at the time of post mortem, cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera of the deceased was preserved.

11. During the course of argument, learned AGA produced the viscera report and from its perusal it appears that no poison was found, therefore, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that due to corona deceased died and as she died due to corona, therefore, after taking permission of the informant, he initiated the cremation proceeding but subsequently informant and his family members intercepted him and lodged the FIR of the present case, cannot be completely disbelieved, at this stage.
12. Further, after viscera report of the deceased, at this stage, it cannot be said that deceased died abnormal death as per the provision of section 304 B IPC.

Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62626274/
2 13.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant who is although husband of the deceased is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant-Tinku, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 18.7.2023 Ankita  Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62626274/
